metadata.technology_specification: Triple quadrupole liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) system
metadata.technology_reasoning: Triple quadrupole LC-MS/MS systems are the industry-standard analytical instruments for targeted quantitative mass spectrometry, widely adopted in pharmaceutical, environmental, and clinical labs for their high sensitivity and selectivity through three sequential quadrupoles for precursor ion selection, fragmentation, and product ion detection.

components.reasoning: This module separates complex mixtures before mass analysis and is a distinct, standard functional unit in LC-MS systems.
The ion source generates charged analyte ions from liquid eluate; ESI is the most common ionization method in LC-MS/MS with its own separate assembly.

Three sequential quadrupoles form the core of the triple quadrupole MS, each responsible for precursor ion selection, fragmentation (collision cell), and product ion filtering; always separate subassemblies.
The collision cell induces fragmentation of selected precursor ions and is a major subcomponent often considered a distinct functional unit inside the second quadrupole.
Maintains high vacuum environment critical for ion transmission and mass analysis; vacuum pumps and chambers are essential, separate from electronic modules.

components.component: Detector Module (e.g., Electron Multiplier or Microchannel Plate)
components.reasoning: Detects ions after mass filtering; a discrete sensitive electronic module with dedicated supply chain and critical function.
Includes consoles and digital electronics for instrument control, signal processing, and data acquisition; separate from mechanical components.
Structural enclosure integrating modules, providing environmental protection and user interface; standard physical component but varies in design.
Automates sample delivery to LC; commonly a distinct module with its own suppliers and critical for throughput.
